body: Reopening this issue to _consider documenting the fix in the Release Notes_.

@junit-team/junit-lambda,

I've added the `team discussion` label to discuss the following in conjunction with this issue as well.

Do we want to completely forbid the use of `@TempDir` on constructor parameters?

Or... should we only forbid that for test instance _per-method_ lifecycle semantics?

In other words, if a developer chooses _per-class_ lifecycle semantics for a given test class, I don't see any problem with using `@TempDir` on a constructor parameter.

Thoughts?

> In other words, if a developer chooses _per-class_ lifecycle semantics for a given test class, I don't see any problem with using `@TempDir` on a constructor parameter.

Seems reasonable. +1

I was very confused when I first used this feature (from the pioneer project). For the record, I very much prefer preventing the use of such extension in the constructor rather than allowing it and passing the same value for each test invocation. 

My preference, of course, would be to allow constructor injection and inject a different value every time the class is instantiated.

Regarding the constructor parameter, when I initially used the `ParameterResolver` I thought that it would be possible to inject into the constructor. Isn't it possible to use that or maybe a new `ConstructorParameterResolver` that would allow passing parameters to the constructor?

> Regarding the constructor parameter, when I initially used the `ParameterResolver` I thought that it would be possible to inject into the constructor. Isn't it possible to use that or maybe a new `ConstructorParameterResolver` that would allow passing parameters to the constructor?

Parameter resolution for constructors via the `ParameterResolver` extension API is not a problem in and of itself.

For example, that works fine with things like `TestInfo` and `TestReporter`. It also works fine for frameworks like the Spring Framework, since Spring looks up the component in the current `ApplicationContext`.

Parameter resolution for constructors only becomes "unintuitive" (i.e., has undesirable side effects) if the resolved argument is stored in the `ExtensionContext.Store`, which is what an extension like `TempDirectory` is basically forced to do.

> I was very confused when I first used this feature (from the pioneer project). 

I can fully understand the confusion.

It's _confusing_ for the core members of the JUnit 5 team as well.

> For the record, I very much prefer preventing the use of such extension in the constructor rather than allowing it and passing the same value for each test invocation.

Thanks for the feedback on that point. That's also our preference and thus the rationale behind disallowing `@TempDir` on constructor parameters for the time being (though potentially re-allowing them if the test class is configured with test instance per-class lifecycle semantics).

> My preference, of course, would be to allow constructor injection and inject a different value every time the class is instantiated.

We (the JUnit 5 team) would also prefer that. It makes the most sense in terms of user expectations.

I actually prototyped a bit locally to see if I could come up with a solution along those lines.

Unfortunately, it is by no means easy to achieve that with the current implementation of the internals of JUnit Jupiter (with regard to scoping of `ExtensionContext` types). Basically, the `ClassExtensionContext` (which is passed to a `ParameterResolver`) does not have access to the `ExtensionContext.Store` that is used by the `MethodExtensionContext`. Consequently, a `ParameterResolver` has no reliable way of providing a temp directory that is _scoped_ for the current test method.

One can argue that this is a flaw in the design/implementation of JUnit Jupiter. In any case, that is the status quo, and it's too late to make drastic changes along those lines in 5.4. So we'll have to see if we can make any improvements on this front in the 5.5+ timeline.

For the time being, field injection is likely the best option -- unless we decide to allow `@TempDir` on constructor parameters for _per-class_ lifecycle semantics prior to the 5.4 GA release.

> @junit-team/junit-lambda,
> 
> I've added the `team discussion` label to discuss the following in conjunction with this issue as well.
> 
> Do we want to completely forbid the use of `@TempDir` on constructor parameters?
> 
> Or... should we only forbid that for test instance _per-method_ lifecycle semantics?
> 
> In other words, if a developer chooses _per-class_ lifecycle semantics for a given test class, I don't see any problem with using `@TempDir` on a constructor parameter.
> 
> Thoughts?

In the interest of simplicity and consisteny I would prefer a complete ban of `@TempDir` on constructor parameters rather than the 'mixed' solution.
